label: The centered interaction model: Y equals beta zero plus beta T times T plus beta A times (age minus 50) plus beta T-A times T times (age minus 50) plus epsilon; with age centered at 50, beta T is the treatment effect at age 50 and beta T-A is the change in the treatment effect per year of age

The uncentered interaction model: Y equals beta zero plus beta T times T plus beta A times age plus beta T-A times T times age plus epsilon; with age uncentered, beta T is the extrapolated effect at age zero and beta T-A is the change in the effect per year
The effect-modification line: the treatment effect at age a, Delta of a, equals E sub 50 plus m times (a minus 50) — a straight line in age whose slope m is the interaction coefficient
The crossover age a star equals 50 minus E sub 50 over m — the age at which the treatment effect crosses zero, where it switches from helping to harming

The 95 percent confidence interval for the interaction coefficient: beta T-A hat plus or minus 1.96 times its standard error; the smallest detectable interaction at the 5 percent level is about 1.96 times this standard error
